text: In the cave, Silas Crane stood at the under-lamp with the stolen key, counting, the way she used to.
He did not hear the water move behind him. A yellow coat, the one Gus had left on the rocks.
The paper said bearer, Silas. Tonight, I am bearing it.
She put the contract into the flame of the low lamp, and the lamp went out with it.
There was a sound like a wave pulling back across stones. When the green light settled, Crane was gone.
Only his shadow was left, on the cave wall. And it was still smiling.
